info.name: retailcloud Console Service API - CRUD Collection
info.description:
Auto-generated from the rc-console-service OpenAPI spec (v1.48.7). Covers Create / List / Get / Replace (PUT) / Update (PATCH) / Delete for every resource in the spec (Business location hierarchy, Catalog classification, Table Setup, KDS Routing, and more), plus the handful of endpoints that don't fit that shape (bulk/batch actions, delete-only nested rows, read-only lookups) grouped alongside their parent resource.

How to use:
1. Set `base_url` (Local: http://localhost:8082/console, UAT: https://uat-api.retailcloud.com/console, Production: https://api.retailcloud.com/console) and `access_token` (Bearer token).
2. Run a resource's folder top-to-bottom — Create captures the new record's id into a collection variable (e.g. {{store_id}}) that the rest of that folder's requests reuse. This API returns each resource with its OWN id field name (storeID, commissaryID, venueID, plain id, ...) rather than a consistent envelope, so the Create request's test script scans the response for whichever key is literally 'id' or ends in 'ID' and captures that.
3. A few endpoints don't fit classic CRUD and are labeled accordingly: 'Stores by Venue' and 'Latest Event' are read-only convenience lookups; 'Bulk Update Tables' and 'Batch Update Order Routing' are action endpoints with no id-based lifecycle; 'Table Group Assignments', 'Routing Setups', and 'Routing Setup Details' are delete-only nested rows (their parent — Table Group / Order Routing Setup — is where they actually get created, as part of that payload).
4. Table Group's PUT is on the collection path itself (no {id} in the URL) — the spec is explicit that 'tableGroupID is supplied in the body, not the path.'

Field values inside request bodies referencing other resources (venue.venueID, zone.id, deliveryLocation.id, admin.userID, etc.) are the spec's own curated example ids — update them to real ids from your environment before running, since they aren't chained automatically.
